source: Liu, Qu, Schneider, Singh, Kumar (2025) CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough
finding: Defines learned termination: at each step the policy picks continue or terminate. Goal is to maximise reward of the final answer, discounted by a per-step cost, over at most T steps.
numbers: Objective: max E[ sum_t gamma^t * 1{a_t=terminate} * R(y,y*) ], gamma in (0,1]. Policy sees prompt x, thoughts z_0:t, observations o_0:t.
quote: strategically gather relevant information over multiple rounds of interaction
limits: Termination is judged only against a fixed information-seeking policy; question quality is not co-optimised.
agent_relevance: This is the formal statement of S8 stop-or-continue: a value-of-continuing decision, not a confidence read-out.

source: Liu, Qu, Schneider, Singh, Kumar (2025) CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough (method: counterfactuals)
finding: Hard-negative counterfactuals. Find a breakpoint where stopping is right, then build a minimally changed copy where stopping is wrong. Label the first terminate and the copy continue. Aim: break shortcuts such as 'stop when the dialogue is long' or 'stop when the last line sounds confident'.
numbers: Medical: pick prefixes where one Q/A pair lifts success by >=50%; counterfactual replaces the last Q/A so success falls below 30%. Math: remove a larger block of reasoning steps because one step is not enough to change success.
limits: Needs a success-rate oracle at every prefix (many rollouts) to label data.
agent_relevance: Our scaffold could build the same pairs offline from logged runs to test a stop rule, without training.

source: Liu, Qu, Schneider, Singh, Kumar (2025) CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough (method: reasoning traces)
finding: Each terminate/continue label is paired with a written reason (GPT-4o generated) that weighs what is known against what is missing. Authors call this a verbalised value function. Trained by SFT; an optional GRPO stage uses reward +1 for a correct decision (success>=0.5 means terminate) and -1 otherwise.
numbers: SFT on counterfactual pairs; RL variant with binary reward. Base: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct (medical), Qwen3-1.7B (math).
limits: RL variant drifted to longer conversations and gave no gain in math.
agent_relevance: Comparative reasoning (stop vs continue side by side) is a prompt pattern usable at S8 even with no fine-tuning; untested without training.

source: Liu, Qu, Schneider, Singh, Kumar (2025) CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough (medical setup)
finding: Interactive diagnosis. A fine-tuned Qwen2.5-3B asks questions; the termination model decides after each Q/A pair. Score is the diagnostic accuracy of an external model (Llama3.1-8B) at the stop point.
numbers: Train: 1,233 diagnosis problems (MedQA-USMLE subset of craft-MD plus MedMCQA), GPT-4o simulated chats. Test: 100 in-distribution plus 200 out-of-distribution dermatology questions; 20 Q/A turns per chat; CI over 30 eval runs and 3 training runs.
limits: Simulated patients (GPT-4o), small 3B models, labels from one small diagnostic model.
agent_relevance: Evidence is simulated; not clinical.

source: Liu, Qu, Schneider, Singh, Kumar (2025) CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough (results medical)
finding: CaRT beat the base model and SFT on mean success rate, difference from a matched-mean fixed budget, and optimal-termination rate. Base and SFT sat on or near the fixed-budget line. It held on out-of-distribution dermatology with a smaller gap. Exact values appear only in plots.
numbers: Text gives no table; plots show success rate about 0.24-0.37 across termination index 6-18; optimal termination rate axis up to about 0.3.
limits: Numbers read from figures, not tables; effect sizes unreported.
agent_relevance: Learned stopping beat a fixed step budget at equal average length: adaptivity is the gain, not shortness.

source: Liu, Qu, Schneider, Singh, Kumar (2025) CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough (results math)
finding: On AIME 2025, CaRT reached higher success with fewer test-time tokens than base and SFT, and aligned best with oracle stop points. RL added length without gain.
numbers: Trained on 2,000 DeepScaleR-preview problems, Qwen3-1.7B traces, 10 episode prefixes each; 3 seeds x 16 evaluations. Episodes split at strategy-change sentences.
limits: Small model; AIME has 30 items so noise is large; no table values in text.
agent_relevance: Stop points at episode boundaries is a ready design for S0/S8 checkpoints.

source: Liu, Qu, Schneider, Singh, Kumar (2025) CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough (ablations)
finding: Counterfactual data gave the largest gain; reasoning traces added consistent smaller gains. An auxiliary confidence score helped SFT and SFT+CF slightly but not the full method. Confidence threshold used: >=0.8. SFT with terminate-label ratio 5-20% did not close the gap. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini were included as off-the-shelf comparisons.
numbers: Ablations: -CF, -reason, +conf, terminate ratio 5/10/15/20%; Qwen3-1.7B needed CF more than Qwen2.5-3B because its traces are longer.
limits: Confidence is not refuted as a stop signal; it was just redundant here.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on a verbal confidence number alone for stopping.

source: Liu, Qu, Schneider, Singh, Kumar (2025) CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough (probe)
finding: Linear probes on hidden states: the reasoning-trained CaRT separates terminate from continue better than the no-reasoning variant and the base model, on train and test splits. Reasoning smooths the termination-rate curve over turns.
numbers: Probe accuracy shown in a figure only (no exact text numbers); compares base, CaRT -reason, full CaRT.
limits: Correlational; separability is not proof of a value function.
agent_relevance: Suggests reasons-before-decision shapes the decision, supporting write-then-decide slots.

source: Wald (1945) Sequential tests of statistical hypotheses; Chow, Robbins, Siegmund (1971) Great Expectations; optimal stopping theory
finding: Classical background cited by CaRT: optimal stopping and sequential tests. A rational stop rule needs the value of continuing, estimated from a value function.
numbers: Not opened this session; no numbers recorded.
limits: Assumes known dynamics; the CaRT paper says this limits open-ended use.
agent_relevance: Gives vocabulary (stopping rule, continuation value) for S8.

source: Chen, Xu, Liang et al. (2024) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Names and measures overthinking. In most responses the first solution is already right and later rounds add nothing. Self-training on First-Correct-Solution data cut tokens with accuracy kept.
numbers: First round correct in >92% of cases (QwQ, R1 on ASDIV, MATH500); first round under 60% of tokens; one example 39 of 901 tokens = 4.3% outcome efficiency; MATH500 on QwQ-32B-Preview: tokens down 48.6% at same accuracy.
quote: In more than 92% of cases, the initial round of solutions produces the correct answer.
limits: Efficiency metric needs the ground truth to find the first correct answer.
agent_relevance: Supports a stop gate after the first verified answer (G3 still applies: verify on a held-out check).

source: Zhang, Lin, Hou, Feng, Li (2025) AdaptThink: Reasoning Models Can Learn When to Think
finding: RL teaches the model to choose NoThinking or Thinking per problem by difficulty. Easy items skip the thinking.
numbers: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B: response length -53%, accuracy +2.4% on math. Table 1 row: AdaptThink accuracy 91.0, length 309, 99.6% NoThinking on an easy set.
limits: Decision made once up front, not during reasoning; needs RL.
agent_relevance: Cheap up-front routing of easy items (S0) is a second kind of learned termination.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models (DEER)
finding: Training-free. At reasoning transition points, force a trial answer and exit if the model is confident in it.
numbers: 11 LRMs, 10 benchmarks: CoT length -19.1% to -80.1%, accuracy +0.3 to +5.0. Qwen3-14B: avg accuracy 83.7 vs 82.8 vanilla at 57.1% of tokens; QwQ-32B: 84.0 vs 82.6 at 80.9% of tokens. NoThinking on Qwen3-14B AIME: 26.7 vs 70.0 vanilla.
quote: monitors model behavior at potential reasoning transition points
limits: Confidence is the model's own token probability; gains on some sets are within noise.
agent_relevance: Training-free trial-answer-then-check is the closest direct recipe for S8 without training.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Know When They're Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification
finding: Linear probe on hidden states predicts whether an intermediate answer is correct. Used as a stop rule it cut tokens with no loss. Some information is present before the answer is written.
numbers: ROC-AUC above 0.7 and ECE below 0.1 in-distribution; generalises across domains on R1-Distill-Llama-8B; early exit saves up to 24% tokens; probe degrades a lot on short-CoT models.
quote: reducing the number of inference tokens by 24% without compromising performance
limits: Needs white-box hidden states; AUC above 0.7 is modest.
agent_relevance: API-only agents cannot use probes; a black-box proxy (answer agreement) is needed.

source: Liu and Wang (2025) Answer Convergence as a Signal for Early Stopping in Reasoning
finding: Models typically reach their final answer after about 60% of reasoning steps. Three tools: stop on repeated same answer, raise end-of-thought probability, and a probe trained to say when to stop.
numbers: Five benchmarks, five open models; on NaturalQuestions Answer Consistency cuts tokens by over 40% and improves accuracy.
quote: models typically converge to their final answers after 60% of the reasoning steps
limits: Stopping on repeated answers can lock in a repeated wrong answer; same-model repeats are not independent (G4).
agent_relevance: Repeat-answer stop is easy code, but treat as a hint only.

source: Li et al. (2024) Escape Sky-high Cost: Early-Stopping Self-Consistency (ESC)
finding: Sample in windows; stop once a whole window agrees. Cuts samples with similar accuracy.
numbers: Sampling reduction: MATH -33.8%, GSM8K -80.1%, StrategyQA -76.8%, CommonsenseQA -78.5%, Coin Flip -84.2%.
limits: Agreement among samples of one model is correlated; fine for cost, weak as proof.
agent_relevance: Window-agreement stop for best-of-N loops.

source: Aggarwal et al. (2023) Let's Sample Step by Step: Adaptive-Consistency
finding: Dirichlet model of answer counts gives a Bayesian stopping criterion for sampling.
numbers: 17 datasets, 3 LLMs: sample budget cut by up to 7.9 times with average accuracy drop under 0.1%.
limits: Same independence caveat as ESC.
agent_relevance: A principled stopping score for our vote loop, computed in code (G5).

source: Fu et al. (2025) Deep Think with Confidence (DeepConf)
finding: Uses internal confidence to drop or stop low-quality traces during parallel thinking.
numbers: AIME 2025 DeepConf@512: up to 99.9% accuracy with up to 84.7% fewer generated tokens versus full parallel thinking.
limits: Needs token log-probs; the headline is the best case.
agent_relevance: Confidence-gated trace stopping where logprobs exist.

source: Hassid et al. (2025) Don't Overthink it: Preferring Shorter Thinking Chains
finding: Longer chains are not better. The shortest of several answers beats random and longest ones.
numbers: Shortest answer beats random by up to 18.8% and longest by up to 34.5% across 4 reasoning LLMs and 4 benchmarks.
limits: Short and correct is partly confounded by easy items.
agent_relevance: Weak support for stopping sooner; do not use length as a vote key without difficulty control.

source: Aggarwal and Welleck (2025) L1: Controlling How Long A Reasoning Model Thinks (LCPO)
finding: RL trains a model to obey a requested token budget, allowing a smooth accuracy-versus-compute trade-off.
numbers: 1.5B L1 surpasses GPT-4o at equal reasoning length; beats S1 length control.
limits: Budget is given, not decided by the model; hard length caps generalise poorly (as CaRT notes).
agent_relevance: Shows budgets can be set from outside; our program owns the budget.

source: Joren et al. (2025) Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
finding: Defines whether context is enough to answer. Big models answer well when context is sufficient but give wrong answers instead of abstaining when it is not. Small models hallucinate or abstain even when sufficient. Sufficiency-guided abstention helps.
numbers: Selective generation raises the correct fraction among answered by 210% for Gemini, GPT and Gemma (abstract).
limits: Sufficiency labelled by an autorater LLM; the figure is a relative gain.
agent_relevance: Same question as CaRT in RAG form: 'do I know enough' as a separate check before answering.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts: Uncertainty-Aware Planning Enhances Information Seeking
finding: Chooses the next question by simulated information gain; improves which question is asked, not a learned stop rule.
numbers: Average +38.1% task completion over direct prompting on medical diagnosis, troubleshooting, 20 Questions.
limits: Studies which question to ask; stopping is by a fixed rule.
agent_relevance: Pairs with CaRT: ask by information gain, stop by learned rule.

source: Gap note: replications of CaRT
finding: No independent replication or failed replication of CaRT was found this session. Semantic Scholar, arXiv and OpenAlex APIs were rate-limited, so forward-citation search was one web query only.
numbers: None found.
limits: Absence here is not proof of absence.
agent_relevance: Treat CaRT as single-source [S].
